items.en: The First Detachment: The Body Reduced to Bone and Light
items.zh: 初背捨 · 內有色相外觀色
parent: The Eight Forms of Detachment: Naming, Stages, and Method
八背捨 · 釋名 · 次位 · 觀法不同

zh: 第四、明修證。行者欲修八背捨無漏觀行，必須精持五篇諸戒，極令清淨。復當精勤勇猛，大誓莊嚴，心無退沒，及能成辦大事。所言初背捨者，不壞內外色，不內外滅色相已，是不淨心觀色，是名初背捨。所以者何？眾生有二分行：愛行、見行。愛多者，著樂，多縛在外結使；見多者，多著身見等諸見，為內結使縛。以是故，愛多者，觀外身不淨；見多者，觀內身不淨敗壞。今明背捨觀行，多先從內起，內觀既成，然後以不淨心觀外。
en: Fourth, clarifying cultivation and realization. The practitioner wishing to cultivate the eight forms of detachment's own undefiled contemplative practice must diligently uphold the five divisions of the precepts, bringing them to the utmost purity. One should, further, be diligent and vigorous, adorned with a great vow, the mind never retreating or sinking, and able to bring this great matter to completion.

As for the first detachment: without yet destroying either the internal or external form, and without having extinguished the mark of internal or external form, one uses this very impure mind to contemplate form — this is named the first detachment. Why is this? Sentient beings divide into two kinds of conduct: the conduct of craving, and the conduct of view. Those in whom craving predominates are attached to pleasure, bound for the most part by fetters that are external; those in whom view predominates are, for the most part, attached to the view of a bodily self and every other such view, bound by fetters that are internal. For this reason, one in whom craving predominates contemplates the external body's own impurity, while one in whom view predominates contemplates the internal body's own impurity and decay. Here, in clarifying the contemplative practice of detachment, one generally begins first from within — once the internal contemplation is accomplished, one then uses this impure mind to contemplate what is external.

zh: 云何觀內？行者端身正心，諦觀足大拇指，想如大豆脹黑，亦如脚繭之相。於靜心中，觀此相成，即復想脹起如梨豆大，如是乃至見一拇指脚如鷄卵大。次觀二指，三、四、五指亦然。次觀脚法，復見腫脹，乃至脚心、脚踵、脚踝、𨄔膝、髀臗，悉見腫脹。次觀右脚亦如是。復當靜心諦想大小便道、腰脊、腹背、胸脇，悉見腫脹。復當靜心諦觀左胛、臂肘、腕掌、五指，悉見腫脹，乃至右胛亦復如是。復當靜心諦觀頸項、頭頷，悉見腫脹。舉身項直，如是從頭至足，從足至頭，循身觀察，但見腫脹，心生厭惡。復當觀壞膿爛，血污不淨，大小便道蟲膿流出。腹既坼破，見諸內臟及三十六物臭爛不淨，心生厭惡，自觀己身甚於死狗，觀外所愛男女之身亦復如是，不可愛樂。廣說如九想，但除散、燒二想為異耳。
en: How does one contemplate what is within? The practitioner, body upright and mind correct, closely contemplates the big toe, imagining it swollen and blackened like a large bean, or like a callus upon the foot. Within the stilled mind, once this mark is accomplished in contemplation, one then imagines it swelling further, the size of a small pear-shaped bean, and so on, until the single big toe is seen as large as a hen's egg. Next, one contemplates the second toe, and the third, fourth, and fifth toes in just the same way. Next, one contemplates the foot itself, seeing it, too, swollen, all the way through the sole, heel, ankle, shin, knee, and thigh, all seen swollen in turn. Next, one contemplates the right foot in just the same way. One should, further, with a stilled mind, closely imagine the passages of urination and defecation, the waist and spine, the belly, back, chest, and flanks, all seen swollen. One should, further, with a stilled mind, closely contemplate the left shoulder blade, arm, elbow, wrist, palm, and five fingers, all seen swollen, and the right shoulder blade in just the same way. One should, further, with a stilled mind, closely contemplate the neck and nape, the head and jaw, all seen swollen. The whole body rigid, neck upright — in this way, from the head down to the feet, and from the feet back up to the head, one contemplates the body in sequence, seeing only swelling, the mind giving rise to weariness and revulsion.

One should, further, contemplate its decay and festering, blood and filth impure, worms and pus flowing out from the passages of urination and defecation. The belly already split open, one sees the internal organs and the thirty-six substances themselves, stinking, rotten, and impure, the mind giving rise to weariness and revulsion, contemplating one's own body as worse even than a dead dog — and contemplating in just the same way the body of any man or woman one loves in the outside world, no longer anything at all to love or delight in. This is explained at greater length as in the nine contemplations, differing only in that the perceptions of scattering and burning are omitted here.

zh: 行者修此觀時，若欲界煩惱未息，當久住此觀中，令厭心純熟。若離貪愛，是時應當進觀白骨，一心靜定，諦觀眉間，想皮肉裂開，見白骨如爪大，的的分明。次當以心向上，裂開皮肉，即見額骨及髮際骨㘈然而開，即見骨相。復觀頂骨，亦見皮肉脫落，髑髏骨出。復當定心，從頭向下，想皮肉皆隨心漸漸剝落至足。皮肉既脫，但見骨人節節相拄，端坐不動。行者爾時即定心，諦觀此骨從因緣生，依因指骨以拄足骨，依因足骨以拄踝骨，依因踝骨以拄𨄔骨，依因𨄔骨以拄膝骨，依因膝骨以拄髀骨，依因髀骨以拄臗骨，依因臗骨以拄腰骨，依因腰骨以拄脊骨，依因脊骨以拄肋骨。復因脊骨上拄項骨，依因項骨以拄頷骨，依因頷骨以拄牙齒，上有髑髏。復因項骨以拄肩骨，依因肩骨以拄臂骨，依因臂骨以拄腕骨，依因腕骨以拄掌骨，依因掌骨以拄指骨。如是展轉相依，有三百六十骨，一一諦觀，知大知小，知強知軟，共相依假，是中無主無我，何者是身見？出入息但是風氣，亦復非身非我，觀受、觀心乃至觀法，悉知虛誑，無主無我。作此觀已，即破我見，憍慢、五欲亦皆除滅。
en: Should the practitioner, cultivating this contemplation, find the desire realm's own afflictions not yet stilled, one should abide within this contemplation for a long while, until the mind of weariness grows fully mature. Once free of craving and attachment, one should, at this time, advance to contemplating the white bones. One-pointedly still in concentration, one closely contemplates the space between the eyebrows, imagining the skin and flesh splitting open, seeing the white bone the size of a fingernail, utterly distinct and clear. Next, directing the mind upward, the skin and flesh split further open, and one sees the forehead bone and the bone at the hairline opening apart, and the very mark of bone is seen. One further contemplates the crown bone, likewise seeing the skin and flesh fall away, the skull itself exposed.

One should, further, with the mind in concentration, moving from the head downward, imagine the skin and flesh, following the mind, gradually peeling away all the way down to the feet. The skin and flesh having fallen away, one sees only a figure of bone, joint resting upon joint, sitting upright and unmoving. The practitioner, at that moment, with the mind in concentration, closely contemplates that these bones arise from causes and conditions: depending upon the toe bones, the foot bones rest upon them; depending upon the foot bones, the ankle bones rest upon them; depending upon the ankle bones, the shin bones rest upon them; depending upon the shin bones, the knee bones rest upon them; depending upon the knee bones, the thigh bones rest upon them; depending upon the thigh bones, the hip bones rest upon them; depending upon the hip bones, the waist bones rest upon them; depending upon the waist bones, the spinal bones rest upon them; depending upon the spinal bones, the rib bones rest upon them. The spinal bones, further, rest the neck bones above them; depending upon the neck bones, the jaw bones rest upon them; depending upon the jaw bones, the teeth rest upon them, and above them the skull itself. The neck bones, further, rest the shoulder bones upon them; depending upon the shoulder bones, the arm bones rest upon them; depending upon the arm bones, the wrist bones rest upon them; depending upon the wrist bones, the palm bones rest upon them; depending upon the palm bones, the finger bones rest upon them. Resting upon one another in succession in just this way, there are three hundred and sixty bones in all — contemplating each one closely, knowing it as large or small, as hard or soft, resting together upon one another provisionally — within this, there is no master, no self at all: what, then, could be called a view of a bodily self? The breath entering and leaving is merely the movement of air, likewise neither body nor self; contemplating sensation, contemplating mind, and, further still, contemplating every dharma, one knows them all to be empty and illusory, without master, without self. Having performed this contemplation, one thereby breaks through the view of self, and arrogance and the five desires, too, are altogether extinguished.

zh: 爾時復當定心，從頭至足，從足至頭，循身諦觀，深鍊白骨，乃經百千許，遍骨人筋骨既盡，骨色如珂如貝，深觀不已，即見骨上白光煜爚。見是相已，即當諦觀眉間，當觀時亦見白光焴焴，悉來趣心。行者不取光相，但定心眉間。若心恬然，任運自住，善根開發，即於眉間見八色光明旋轉而出，遍照十方，皆悉明淨。八色者，謂地、水、火、風、青、黃、赤、白。普照大地，見地色如黃白淨地，見水色如淵中澄清之水，見火色如無煙薪清淨之火，見風色如無塵清風，見青色如金精山，見黃色如薝蔔華，見赤色如春朝霞，見白色如珂雪，隨是色相，悉有光耀。雖復見色分明，而無形質可得，此色超勝，非世所有。是相發時，行者心定安隱，喜樂無量，不可文載也。
en: At that time, one should, further, with the mind in concentration, from the head down to the feet, and from the feet back up to the head, contemplate the body closely in sequence, deeply refining the figure of bone, continuing on through some hundred or thousand repetitions, until, throughout the figure of bone, its sinews are entirely gone, the bones' own color like agate, like shell — contemplating still more deeply without pause, one then sees a white light shimmering upon the bones themselves. Having seen this mark, one should closely contemplate the space between the eyebrows; contemplating there, one likewise sees a bright white light, all converging toward the mind. The practitioner does not grasp at this mark of light, but simply keeps the mind in concentration at the space between the eyebrows. Should the mind grow calm and still, resting naturally of its own accord, the wholesome root opens forth, and, at the space between the eyebrows, eight colors of light are seen, spinning forth and radiating, illuminating the ten directions entirely, everywhere bright and pure.

The eight colors are: earth, water, fire, wind, blue-green, yellow, red, and white. Illuminating the great earth everywhere, one sees the color of earth like a pure yellow-white ground; one sees the color of water like clear, still water within a deep pool; one sees the color of fire like a smokeless, pure flame of burning wood; one sees the color of wind like a dustless, pure breeze; one sees the color blue-green like a mountain of refined gold; one sees the color yellow like a campaka blossom; one sees the color red like the morning glow of spring's own dawn; one sees the color white like agate or snow — following each of these colors' own marks, each, in turn, possesses its own radiance. Though one sees these colors distinctly, they possess no material substance whatsoever to be found — this color transcends and surpasses, nothing of its kind found anywhere in the world. When this mark arises, the practitioner's mind is settled and at peace, joy and happiness beyond measure, impossible to record fully in writing.

zh: 行者復當從頭至足，深鍊骨人，還復攝心，諦觀於額，住心緣中。復見八色光明旋轉而出。如是次第定心，觀髮際、頂、兩耳孔、眉骨、眼骨、鼻、口、齒、頷骨、頸項骨。從上至下，三百六十諸骨諸節，悉見八色光明旋轉而出。行者攝心轉細，從頭至足，從足至頭，觀此骨人，悉見遍身放光，普照一切，悉皆明淨。若是菩薩大士，咸於光中見諸佛像；若行人善根劣弱，乃至四禪，方得見諸佛像。行者既光明照耀，定心喜樂，倍上所得，是名證初背捨相。所以者何？內骨人未滅故，故名內有色相，見外八種光明及欲界不淨境故，故言以是不淨心觀外色。外色有二種，如欲界不淨，此是不淨外色。八種清淨之色，是出世間色界之色，故名外色。行者見內外不淨色故，背捨欲界，心不喜樂。見八種淨色故，即知根本初禪無明暗蔽，虛誑不實，境界麁劣，即能棄捨，心不染著，故論言：「背是淨潔五欲，離是著心，故名背捨。」
en: The practitioner should, further, from the head down to the feet, deeply refine the figure of bone once more, again gathering the mind, closely contemplating the forehead, the mind fixed upon its own object. Once more, eight colors of light are seen, spinning forth. In this way, in due sequence, with the mind in concentration, one contemplates the hairline, the crown, the two ear-openings, the brow bone, the eye sockets, the nose, mouth, teeth, jaw bone, and neck bone. From the top downward, all three hundred and sixty bones and joints are seen, each giving forth the eight colors of light, spinning forth in turn. The practitioner, gathering the mind ever more finely, from the head down to the feet, and from the feet back up to the head, contemplates this figure of bone, seeing the whole body radiating light, illuminating everything, entirely bright and pure. Should this be a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, buddha-images themselves are seen within this very light; should the practitioner's own wholesome root be weak and inferior, it is only upon reaching the fourth dhyāna that buddha-images come to be seen at all. The practitioner, the light now radiant, the mind in concentration joyful and happy, redoubled beyond what was obtained before — this is named realizing the mark of the first detachment.

Why is this? Because the internal figure of bone has not yet been extinguished, this is named "form-mark within"; because one sees the eight kinds of external light together with the desire realm's own impure objects, it is said: using this impure mind, one contemplates form without. External form is of two kinds: impurity such as the desire realm's own — this is impure external form; the eight kinds of pure color are the color belonging to the world-transcending form realm — this, too, is named external form. The practitioner, seeing both internal and external impure form, thereby turns away from the desire realm, the mind no longer taking delight in it. Seeing the eight kinds of pure color, one thereby knows that the root first dhyāna is itself obscured by ignorance, empty and unreal, its own objects coarse and inferior, and is thereby able to relinquish it, the mind no longer stained by attachment to it — hence the treatise says: "Turning one's back on the pure and unblemished five desires, relinquishing the attached mind — this is named detachment."

zh: 復次，如《摩訶衍》中說初禪一背捨，當知背捨即是無漏初禪。若是初禪，即便具有五支之義，今當分別。如行者從初不淨觀來，乃至鍊骨人光耀，即是觀禪欲界定相；次攝心眉間，泯然定住，即是觀禪未到地相；八種光明旋轉而出，覺此八色昔所未見，心大驚悟，即是觀禪覺支之相。分別八色，其相各異，非世所有，即是觀支；慶心踊躍，即是喜支；恬憺之法怡悅娛心，即是樂支；雖覩此色，無顛倒想，三昧不動，即是一心支。今略事分別此無漏觀禪五支之相，當知與上根本、特勝、通明中五支條然有異。
en: Furthermore, as explained in the Mahāyāna treatise, the first dhyāna's own single detachment — one should know that detachment is itself precisely the undefiled first dhyāna. Being the first dhyāna, it is thereby complete with the sense of the five factors as well, which shall now be distinguished. As the practitioner, proceeding from the initial contemplation of impurity all the way through the figure of bone's own radiance, this is precisely the mark of contemplative dhyāna's own desire-realm concentration; next, gathering the mind at the space between the eyebrows, resting still and undisturbed in concentration, this is precisely the mark of contemplative dhyāna's own not-yet-arrived state; the eight kinds of light spinning forth, perceiving these eight colors never before seen, the mind greatly startled into awakening — this is precisely the mark of contemplative dhyāna's own factor of initial thought. Distinguishing the eight colors, each mark differing from the rest, found nowhere else in the world — this is precisely the factor of sustained reflection; the mind leaping with delight — this is precisely the factor of joy; the calm and tranquil dharma bringing pleasure and delight to the mind — this is precisely the factor of happiness; though beholding this very color, no inverted perception arises, samādhi unmoved — this is precisely the factor of one-pointedness of mind. This, in brief, distinguishes the mark of this undefiled contemplative dhyāna's own five factors; one should know that these differ markedly from the five factors already given above, within the root dhyānas, the special excellences, and the thorough-and-bright contemplation.

The first detachment reprises fascicle 9's nine contemplations almost exactly (swelling, decay, festering, all the way through skeletonization) before adding something the charnel-ground meditation never reached: once the body is reduced entirely to bone, the practice keeps going, refining the bone itself until it radiates eight colors of light, mapped onto the four elements and four pure hues. This is the treatise's own clearest statement of the difference between the destructive and non-destructive paths in practice, not just in name — the destructive path stops at bones and ash, while this path treats the skeleton as raw material for something further, building an entire second contemplative structure (concentration, near-attainment, and the five dhyāna factors) on top of the same visceral starting point.

quiz.q: What do those of craving-conduct and view-conduct each contemplate?
options: craving: external fetters, contemplate the outer body; view: internal fetters, contemplate the inner body
quiz.why: Those dominated by craving are bound by external fetters and contemplate the outer body; those dominated by views by internal fetters and contemplate the inner body. Detachment generally starts from within.

quiz.q: What must the practitioner have before cultivating the eight detachments?
options: pure keeping of the five sections of precepts, vigor, a great vow, an unretreating mind
quiz.why: One must keep the five divisions of the precepts purely and be vigorous, adorned with a great vow, never retreating.

quiz.q: Where does the contemplation of the inner body begin?
options: the big toe, imagined swollen and black like a bean, growing to an egg, then the other toes and the whole body
quiz.why: One begins with the big toe, imagined swollen and black like a bean, growing to the size of a hen's egg, then the other toes, the foot, and the whole body. The brow comes later for the bones and light.

quiz.q: How does the impurity contemplation of the first detachment differ from the nine contemplations?
options: as in the nine, except that scattering and burning are omitted
quiz.why: It is as in the nine contemplations, except that the perceptions of scattering and burning are omitted.

quiz.q: Contemplating the bones arising from conditions, what does one conclude?
options: 360 bones rest on one another with no master or self; breath too is not self; self-view, conceit, and desires are removed
quiz.why: The 360 bones rest on one another provisionally with no master or self; the breath is only air; this breaks the view of self, and conceit and the five desires are removed.

quiz.q: When does the practitioner advance to contemplating white bones?
options: while afflictions persist one stays with the swelling; once free of craving one advances
quiz.why: If desire-realm afflictions have not subsided, one remains long in this contemplation; once free of craving one advances to the white bones.

quiz.q: After deep refinement of the bones, what first appears, and how should one respond?
options: white light shimmering on the bones; one does not grasp it but keeps the mind at the brow
quiz.why: The bones become like agate and shell, then white light shimmers on them; the practitioner does not grasp at the light but keeps the mind at the brow, after which the eight colors appear.

quiz.q: What are the eight colors issuing from between the brows?
options: earth, water, fire, wind, blue, yellow, red, white
quiz.why: The eight colors are earth, water, fire, wind, blue-green, yellow, red, and white.

quiz.q: Which simile for the eight colors is correct?
options: yellow like a campaka blossom, red like spring dawn, white like agate-snow
quiz.why: Blue-green is like a mountain of refined gold, yellow like a campaka blossom, red like spring dawn, white like agate or snow; water is like a still pool.

quiz.q: How do bodhisattvas and those of weak roots differ in seeing buddha-images in the light?
options: bodhisattvas see them in this light; the weak only upon reaching the fourth dhyāna
quiz.why: Bodhisattvas see buddha-images in the light at once; practitioners of weak roots see them only upon reaching the fourth dhyāna.

quiz.q: Why is the first detachment called "form within"?
options: the inner figure of bone has not yet been extinguished
quiz.why: Because the internal figure of bone has not been extinguished, it is "form within"; because one sees the external light and the impure objects of the desire realm, one "contemplates form without."

quiz.q: What two kinds of external form are there?
options: impure desire-realm form, and the eight pure colors of the world-transcending form realm
quiz.why: External form is the impure form of the desire realm and the eight pure colors, which belong to the world-transcending form realm.

quiz.q: Having seen the eight pure colors, how does the practitioner regard the root first dhyāna?
options: obscured by ignorance, unreal, coarse; one relinquishes it without attachment
quiz.why: Seeing the pure colors, one knows the root first dhyāna to be obscured by ignorance, unreal, and coarse, and relinquishes it without attachment.

quiz.q: In the undefiled first detachment, what is the factor of initial thought?
options: the eight lights spinning forth, never seen before, startling the mind awake
quiz.why: The eight lights spinning forth, never before seen, startling the mind, is initial thought; distinguishing them is sustained reflection; leaping delight is joy; unmoving samādhi is one-pointedness.

quiz.q: What are the desire-realm concentration and not-yet-arrived state of contemplative dhyāna?
options: from impurity to the radiant bones is desire-realm; resting still at the brow is not-yet-arrived
quiz.why: From the initial impurity contemplation through the radiant bones is contemplative dhyāna's desire-realm concentration; gathering the mind at the brow and resting still is its not-yet-arrived state.
